verdict.rationale: Adyen documents its own ways to evaluate risk configurations before rollout: risk experiments that A/B test two risk profiles, and rule backtesting against historical data before going live. However, A/B tests let both profiles make real decisions, and backtesting is a historical replay; neither is a shadow-mode trial on live traffic. No precision or recall metrics for the model are evidenced. Missing for 10: precision/recall measurement on merchant traffic, true shadow-mode trials where new models or rules score live traffic without taking decisions, ML-model-level performance reporting, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can measure the model itself — precision and recall on my traffic, shadow-mode trials of new models or rules before they take over decisions

citations.quote: Risk experiments let you A/B test two risk profiles against each other to determine which performs better.
Risk Rule Backtesting. Test and optimize risk rules against historical data before going live.
